title: 'When He Plays, They Lose More': Jasprit Bumrah Targeted After Lord's Test Defeat
text:
'When He Plays, They Lose More': Jasprit Bumrah Targetted After Lord's Test Defeat
Jasprit Bumrah is slated to play in three of the five Tests of the England series, but David Lloyd said that could change depending on the result of 4th Test.
With India enduring their second defeat of the England tour, the visitors are facing with a familiar question: Should they play Jasprit Bumrah with series on the line or rest him to manage his workload as planned? India started the tour with a defeat in Leeds and despite them trailing, Bumrah was benched and given the performances of his fellow pacers, the decision was criticised. However, Akash Deep and Mohammed Siraj stepped up to claim 16 wickets between them and pulled India on level terms in Birmingham.
At Lord’s, Bumrah returned for the third Test and repeated his heroics of the series opener with his second five-wicket haul of the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy. This time too his effort with the ball went in vain as India suffered their second defeat.

Bumrah, as the Indian team management announced before the tour, will play in three of the five Tests of the series meaning he will either play at Old Trafford where the fourth Test will be held or the fifth at The Oval. Former England cricketer David Lloyd though feels that the plan could change should India manage to draw level in Manchester.
“It is what they’ve said and what the coach Gautam Gambhir said that he will play three out of the five Tests. So, he’s got a choice. There are two matches to go. He’s played two. If they are true to their words, he should play this next game at Old Trafford. But then, you know, they can manoeuvre that, can’t they?" Lloyd said on TalkSport Cricket.
“If he (Bumrah) plays this next one at Old Trafford and they get a result to make it 2-2, you’d think he’d play at The Oval as well. I’m second-guessing, but I think he’ll play this next game and see where they are. If England go 3-1, he won’t play. But if it’s 2-2, he will play at the Oval," he added.
When reminded that India’s only win of the tour came when Bumrah was rested, Lloyd responded, “That’s extraordinary. There was something that said when he (Bumrah) plays, they (India) lose more than when he doesn’t play, and he is like the best bowler in the world. And he is awkward and nasty with his action, but a thoroughly decent fella."
